exercises.title: Build Cedar Court's chart
exercises.intro: The ownership chart names every 20% owner and one control person, down to people (CORE-KYC-02). Multiply percentages through each layer. Sort each party.

buckets: 20% owner or trust party: chart, ID and screen
Screen as a source of funds

items.text: Marcus Hale: 60% of Cedar Court Partners LLC, managing member
items.why: He owns 60%, so he is charted and screened. As managing member he is also the control person (CORE-KYC-02).

items.text: Priya Nand: 40% of Cedar Court Partners LLC
items.bucket: 20% owner or trust party: chart, ID and screen
items.why: 40% is at least 20%, so she is charted, gives ID and is screened (CORE-KYC-01, -02).

items.text: The separate holding LLC whose passive investors supply part of the equity
items.bucket: Screen as a source of funds
items.why: It is a source of funds, not an owner of the borrower. Ask who owns it and screen its 20% owners (CORE-KYC-07; worked example 3).

items.text: What-if: person D owns 40% of a holding LLC that owns 50% of the borrower
items.bucket: 20% owner or trust party: chart, ID and screen

items.text: What-if: person E owns 40% of a holding LLC that owns 40% of the borrower
items.why: 40% × 40% = 16%, under 20% (quiz B5). E is not a 20% owner.

items.text: What-if: trustee T of an irrevocable trust that owns 20% of the borrower
items.bucket: 20% owner or trust party: chart, ID and screen
items.why: A trust holding 20% or more puts every trustee on the chart (CORE-KYC-08; quiz A5).

items.text: What-if: beneficiary C, sole beneficiary of that same 20% irrevocable trust
items.bucket: 20% owner or trust party: chart, ID and screen
items.why: C's look-through share is 100% × 20% = 20%, so C is charted (CORE-KYC-08).

items.text: What-if: the grantor of that irrevocable trust, with no look-through share
items.why: A grantor is charted only for a revocable trust (CORE-KYC-08; quiz A5 key).

exercises.title: Spot the red flags
exercises.intro: CORE-KYC-07 red flags stop the file until the BSA officer clears them. Read each fact and decide whether it stops the loan.

items.text: Maple Run: the house is vacant and will be leased to an unrelated tenant. Dana Reyes lives at a separate Columbus address she owns
items.why: No sign the guarantor will live there (CORE-BP-02; worked example 4).

items.text: Maple Run: the $74,100 cash to close comes from Dana Reyes's own accounts, proved by two statements
items.why: The funds are the guarantor's own, shown by statements (CORE-BOR-13). No third-party money.

items.text: What-if: title shows the Maple Run seller bought the house 7 months ago for $210,000. Our price is $300,000
items.why: 1 − $210,000 ÷ $300,000 = 30.0%, at least 20% within 12 months (CORE-KYC-07). The BSA officer may clear it on evidence.

items.text: What-if: title shows the seller bought the subject 8 months ago for $180,000. Our price is $240,000
items.why: 1 − $180,000 ÷ $240,000 = 25.0%, at least 20% within 12 months (CORE-KYC-07; quiz A7).

items.text: What-if: the day before funding, an email from the title company's address gives a new account number
items.why: Any change to wire instructions is a flag. Call the number already in our file, then escalate (CORE-KYC-07, -05).

items.text: What-if: $400,000 of Birchwood's equity arrives by wire from Lakeshore Capital Partners, not named in the file
items.why: Cash to close from an unrelated third party (CORE-KYC-07). Identify and screen the source and its 20% owners.

items.text: What-if: a guarantor's mail goes to the subject house, and its utilities are in her name
items.why: An occupancy sign: she appears to live at the subject (CORE-BP-02; quiz B7).

items.text: What-if: Leo Marsh's 25% is held through an LLC that is 60% owned by a person on the SDN List
items.why: That LLC is blocked under the 50 Percent Rule [VERIFY: OFAC FAQs 398-401; checked 20 Nov 2026]. It holds an interest in our borrower. Treat it as an unresolved match: stop and escalate (CORE-KYC-01). No exception (CORE-EXC-03).

exercises.title: SAR timeline: days 0, 30 and 60
exercises.intro: What-if (RD-RES-01): on Friday 20 Nov 2026, an email asks us to send Maple Run's $240,000 advance to a new account. The sender is unknown. Put the steps in date order.

steps: Day 0, Fri 20 Nov 2026: call the title company on the number in our file. It confirms it sent no such email. This is first detection
Same business day: report the flag to the BSA officer (CORE-KYC-05)
The BSA officer decides whether to file. The attempt involved $240,000, over the $5,000 threshold, so a SAR is likely
Fri 18 Dec 2026: planned filing date, the last business day before the deadline
Day 30, Sun 20 Dec 2026: normal SAR deadline, 30 calendar days after first detection
Day 60, Tue 19 Jan 2027: outer limit if no suspect is identified
For 5 years from filing: keep the SAR and its support
order.why: Escalate the same day; only the BSA officer decides on a SAR (CORE-KYC-05). The deadline is 30 calendar days after first detection. With no suspect, up to 30 more days are allowed, never more than 60 in all [VERIFY: 31 CFR 1029.320; checked 20 Nov 2026]. Day 30 is a Sunday, so plan to file by Friday 18 Dec. Records are kept 5 years from filing.
